title: Build athena-cap-study crate: study records and validation rules
summary: I read this as building the reusable core of the study capability: a new athena-cap-study crate with the design's typed records, the §5.4 validation rules, and a Capability impl with prompts. The run step, containment, and Pages publishing are left out. The file set is chosen to avoid the admission rules (governance files, size, personal data) that the earlier attempt likely tripped.

defaults_applied.how: The new crate is Rust; its prompts are non-Rust markdown, as in athena-cap-change/prompts.
Each validation rule gets a planted-fault test and a clean-case test; cargo test and clippy must be clean.
Narrowed to the validation core and the crate skeleton instead of the whole design.
Follows the reviewed design docs/design/study-capability-m1.md and its review 2 changes.
Evidence rules are enforced in code and are non-waivable; the verifier's judgments (§5.5) stay marked as prose.
Reuse existing workspace crates (athena-data Quantity, athena-git, serde) and do not build a formal-language checker, per alternative A2-D.
I recovered the scope from the design doc, D64, and the architecture table.
Examples stay synthetic; no secrets or email addresses.

assumptions: Job 9vwq failed admission, which checks governance files, file size, secrets or emails, records/, and classification changes; its log is not available to me. I assume the cause was an unlisted governance file, an oversize file, or personal data, and I avoid all three.

The design (docs/design/study-capability-m1.md) passed review 2 with named changes (R2-m1, R2-m2, R2-m3). I assume the builder applies those: spend-rule wording, a field on study.finding/1 naming what it covers, and added finding kinds.

One job cannot build everything in the design, so I read 'build the study capability' as the reusable validation core: the crate, records, the model, the §5.4 rules, and the Capability impl. Containment, the run step, replay, and Pages publishing are left for later jobs.
The Capability trait in athena-core may not fit a multi-step study job. I assume the crate implements it as-is and any needed trait change is deferred and noted.
The workspace Cargo.toml may list members explicitly. If it only uses a glob, it will not change.
question: Job 9vwq's admission failure record isn't visible to me. Do you want the full design built, or only the validation core as I read it?

acceptance_criteria.text: A new crate crates/athena-cap-study exists with its own Cargo.toml (workspace package/lint inheritance, no edits to any [lints] table) and src/lib.rs, and is a member of the workspace.

The crate defines typed records from design §4 with a schema field: study.pin/1, study.source/1, study.claim/1, study.run/1, study.rationale/1, study.finding/1, study.gap/1, study.validation/1, plus study.model/1 with the §5.1 elements. Numbers are Quantity values (measured or labeled estimate), not bare numbers.

The crate implements the §5.4 validation rules as pure functions over records, each classed evidence (non-waivable) or model (waivable); a waiver clears only a model rule and only when it names the rule and ids and cites a user intervention record.
Rules that need git lookups (Wrong SHA, Bad citation, Quote mismatch) go through a small trait or fixture repository, not the live network.

The crate implements the core Capability trait (id "study", card, producer and verifier prompt sections under crates/athena-cap-study/prompts/) but is NOT registered in athena-cli wiring, and does not run any studied system.
docs/architecture.md gains an athena-cap-study row listing its dependency edges, matching the actual Cargo.toml dependencies.
CHANGELOG.md records the new crate; a decisions.md entry records the scope call (validation core only; containment, run step, and Pages publishing deferred).
Run `cargo test` from the repo root: every §5.4 rule has a test with one planted fault and one clean case, and all tests pass, including existing architecture/dependency tests.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: both clean.

Run `git status` and `git diff --stat`: no change under records/, no governance file (athena.toml, defaults.toml, setup.sh, rust-toolchain.toml, workflows, .gitattributes, rustfmt/clippy config), no file over the size limit, no email addresses.

out_of_scope: Containment, the run step, replay, and any running of a studied system
The Pages explainer design and publish step
Studying firstmate or any real system; pinning a SHA
Registering the capability in athena-cli wiring or athena.toml
Changes to governance files, [lints] tables, or CI workflows
Changing the Capability trait in athena-core, unless unavoidable and noted
departures: Cost and time are above the reference. It adds a new crate with about 17 rules, each with two tests, and the verifier needs a cold full-workspace build. Pass probability is lower because the earlier attempt failed and the scope is large.
